verified_signals.signal: MNB decision H-KPL-I-B-1/2026 (25/03/2026) fines CIB Bank Zrt. verified_signals.signal: MNB decision H-PM-I-B-8/2026 (13/02/2026), a follow-up monitoring the bank's performance of decision H-PM-I-B-1/2025 (03/02/2025), fines Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. HUF 5,000,000 (2 x HUF 2.5m) for AML/CTF breaches and orders remediation by 30/04/2026: a rule and control environment guaranteeing enhanced due diligence for EVERY high-risk client; an IT-supported control environment able to test whether a low-risk classification is justified for clients handled under enhanced due diligence; and a risk-based retrospective review back to 01/01/2023 of the quality of alert pre-screening performed by its outsourced provider (CRISP). verified_signals.entity: Hungary ATM market (MNB payment statistics, via press)
verified_signals.signal: Hungary had 5,688 ATMs at 31/03/2026 versus 5,211 at 31/03/2025 - 477 net new machines, +9.15% YoY. Budapest was DOWN 8 units and county seats up only 6, so essentially all growth was in small settlements. Fastest-growing counties: Szabolcs-Szatmar-Bereg +37.37%, Nograd +36.36%, Borsod-Abauj-Zemplen +24.6%. Budapest still holds 1,419 machines (24.95% of the stock) and Nograd the fewest at 105. Separately sourced: 5,645 ATMs were operating at end-December 2025, +9.8% YoY, against 4,738 at end-2022.
verified_signals.source_name: Bankmonitor, 'Hol telepitettek ATM-et a bankok az elmult evben?' (on MNB payment statistics); end-2025 figure from Bankmonitor, 'Eljohet Magyarorszagon a keszpenz ujabb aranykora?' and BiztosDontes
verified_signals.implies: Quantifies the mandate-driven build-out at roughly 477 net new machines a year, essentially all of it rural. Squarely Printec's ATM/self-service line plus rural managed services (remote monitoring, cash-in-transit-light replenishment). Note the counter-current: Budapest is shrinking, so the urban replacement/consolidation cycle is a separate and opposite motion.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - Phase 2 (settlements over 500 population) due 31/12/2026 sustains the run-rate through this year
verified_signals.followup: Pull the MNB penzforgalmi tablakeszlet Q1-2026 tables directly for the per-institution split and for a properly sourced deposit-capable series; the deposit-capable claim below could not be verified and must not be used until it is.

verified_signals.signal: MBH Bank operates 1,200 ATMs at 1,114 locations (second-largest network in Hungary). It met the ATMtv. Phase 1 obligation in early December 2025, ahead of the 31/12/2025 deadline. During 2025 it commissioned 77 new ATMs in villages of 1,000-2,000 residents, raising coverage there from 189 to 266 settlements (+41%); over the preceding two years it replaced nearly 500 ATMs with more modern machines under a network programme launched at end-2023; and it PLANS 115 FURTHER locations in settlements under 1,000 residents during 2026, on top of the 50 it already serves in that band. Its 2023 programme targets a 52% expansion of total ATM stock by 2026.
verified_signals.source_name: Fintech.hu, 'Tovabb bovult az MBH Bank ATM-halozata'
verified_signals.implies: MBH is the clear over-performer on the mandate and has a named 115-location programme for 2026 plus an ongoing fleet-replacement cycle - concrete hardware, installation and managed-services volume that is being bought now rather than tendered later. No OEM is named anywhere in public sources: identifying MBH's ATM vendor is the single highest-value unknown in this cluster.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - 115 locations are named for 2026 and Phase 2 completion is due 31/12/2026
verified_signals.followup: Identify MBH's incumbent ATM OEM and service provider; target the 115-location 2026 tranche and the replacement cycle. Note MBH is NOT clean with the regulator - it was fined HUF 15m on 07/05/2026 under the cash-handling regime, which is a separate and warmer entry point.

verified_signals.signal: From February 2026 the statutory free monthly ATM cash-withdrawal allowance on Hungarian household forint accounts doubled from HUF 150,000 to HUF 300,000, still capped at two transactions per month and still requiring the customer to file a declaration with one nominated bank; the allowance is usable at any domestic bank's ATM. The law change was published in Magyar Kozlony in December 2025. Banks, not customers, bear the 0.9% cash-withdrawal transaction levy, which is uncapped - so doubling the free ceiling directly increases bank cost per withdrawal. Confirmed still in force in June 2026.
verified_signals.source_name: Bank360, 'Nem tudunk megvalni a keszpenztol: februartol 300 ezer forintot lehet dijmentesen felvenni'
verified_signals.implies: Fewer, larger withdrawals raise cash volume dispensed per machine while the uncapped 0.9% levy raises the marginal cost of every withdrawal to the bank. That strengthens the business case for recyclers and for optimised cash forecasting/replenishment (Printec cash automation and OptiCash-type managed services) over simply adding dispense-only units - which matters because the mandate is pushing banks to install exactly the dispense-only units that are least economic.
verified_signals.followup: Verify against the amending statute in Magyar Kozlony and MNB Q1/Q2-2026 payment data; quantify the levy and cash-logistics cost impact per bank as the core of the recycler business case.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Fetched and parsed the cited article. Independently corroborated as still in force by the Bankmonitor article of 17/06/2026: 'a jogszabalyi ingyenes keszpenzfelvetelt - havi ket alkalom osszesen legfeljebb 300 ezer forint - barmely magyarorszagi ATM-nel ki lehet hasznalni'. verified_signals.entity: OTP Bank / Erste HU / Raiffeisen HU (Constitutional Court challenge)
verified_signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2025] On 10/11/2025 OTP Bank Nyrt. disclosed to the Budapest Stock Exchange that, jointly with several other credit institutions, it had that day filed a constitutional complaint at the Alkotmanybirosag seeking a declaration that provisions of Act XVIII of 2025 (the ATM Act) and the related instruments - NGM decree 16/2025 (V.29.), MNB decree 19/2025 (VI.26.), and MNB decree 1/2023 (I.17.) as amended by MNB decree 20/2025 (VI.26.) - are unconstitutional, arguing the ATM siting and cost-allocation rules are economically unjustified, disproportionately restrict the institutions' freedom of enterprise and property rights, and discriminatorily interfere with market processes. Index reports, on its own information rather than OTP's disclosure, that the co-filers are Erste and Raiffeisen. No ruling published as of 31/07/2026.
verified_signals.source_name: Index.hu, 'Alkotmanybirosaghoz fordul az OTP a kistelepulesek ATM-rendelete miatt' (quoting OTP's BET disclosure)
verified_signals.implies: The challenge is live and has NOT stopped enforcement - the MNB issued four binding orders and a fine on 25/03/2026 regardless. Banks must keep buying and installing while litigating. Critically, the complaint also attacks MNB decree 1/2023 as amended, which is the banknote-validator and cash-machine availability regime underpinning the sector-wide compliance signal below - so a strike-down would deflate BOTH the Phase 2 installation pipeline and the validator/uptime services pipeline. This is the single largest risk to the Hungarian pipeline.
verified_signals.likelihood: Medium - filed and pending; no ruling published as of 31/07/2026 and no hearing date public
verified_signals.win: n/a - macro risk driver, not a pursuable deal
verified_signals.followup: Monitor alkotmanybirosag.hu for the case number and any decision; treat a strike-down as the principal downside scenario for both the Phase 2 and the validator/uptime pipelines.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Fetched and parsed the cited article, which reproduces OTP's Budapest Stock Exchange announcement verbatim. Confirmed the filing date 10/11/2025, the article byline date '2025.11.10. 17:21', and the grounds quoted verbatim ('gazdasagilag indokolatlan, aranytalanul korlatozza a kerelmezo hitelintezetek vallalkozashoz es tulajdonhoz valo alapjogait, tovabba diszkriminativ modon avatkozik bele a piaci folyamatokba'). TWO MATERIAL ADDITIONS the original pass missed. (a) The complaint's scope is broader than 'Act XVIII and the related MNB decree': OTP's own disclosure names NGM decree 16/2025 (V.29.), MNB decree 19/2025 (VI.26.) AND MNB decree 1/2023 (I.17.) as amended by MNB decree 20/2025 (VI.26.). That last item is the validator/availability regime, so the litigation risk cuts across two of this cluster's pipelines, not one. (b) Sourcing caveat: OTP's disclosure says only 'tobb hitelintezettel kozosen' (jointly with several credit institutions) and does NOT name the co-filers; the Erste/Raiffeisen identification is explicitly Index's own unsourced reporting ('Az Index informacioi szerint'). verified_signals.entity: MNB decree 19/2025 (VI.26.) - Phase 2 and reallocation mechanics
verified_signals.signal: Consolidated text of MNB decree 19/2025 (VI.26.), in force from 27/06/2025. Allocation weights: 2024 payment-service fee revenue 20%; debit cards with a cash-withdrawal function issued as at 31/12/2024 30%; consumer payment accounts at 31/12/2024 10%; retail sight forint deposits with a non-zero balance at 31/12/2024 15%; balance-sheet total at 31/12/2024 25% - assessed at group level for banking groups, then overlaid with per-settlement macro criteria (district gross average earnings, settlement population, unemployment rate, share of residents employed off-settlement). Annex 1 names the obligated bank for every affected settlement and IS PUBLIC. Section 3(3)(b): banks wishing to SWAP settlement packages with each other or take over one another's installation/operation duty for the Phase 2 (over-500-population) wave had to sign those INTER-BANK contracts by 28/02/2026 and report them into the MNB's ERA system within 5 working days, and by 16/03/2026 at the latest. Section 3(2): a contract taking over ATM OPERATION cannot be concluded for less than 5 years. Section 4(4): a newly designated operator must reimburse the previous installer's demonstrably incurred installation costs (those incurred within 3 years). Sections 4(3) and 6: the MNB re-runs the whole allocation every 3 years, first review due around 27/06/2028.
verified_signals.implies: Two durable commercial hooks. First, the 5-year minimum term on operation-takeover contracts plus the 3-yearly statutory reallocation means ATM operation in rural Hungary is a recurring, contractually long site-transfer business rather than a one-off install - and the next reallocation lands around mid-2028. Second, the cost-reimbursement rule at s.4(4) means an incoming bank inherits a priced asset, which favours standardised, well-documented estates and a single service partner across banks. Annex 1 being public means Printec can build the full settlement-by-settlement target map today.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - in force, with the next statutory reallocation due around 27/06/2028
verified_signals.followup: Extract the full Annex 1 settlement-to-bank map from jogtar and build the territory plan; note the ERA-reported contract register would only reveal inter-bank reallocations, NOT vendor selections, so it is a lower-value ask than the original pass assumed.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Fetched the consolidated text and read sections 1-7 and Annex 1 in full. Entry into force confirmed ('Hataly: 2025.VI.27. -'). Allocation weights CONFIRMED and made more precise: the 30% is specifically debit cards WITH a cash-withdrawal function at 31/12/2024, the 15% is retail SIGHT forint deposits with a NON-ZERO balance, and all stock measures are as at 31/12/2024 while the fee-revenue measure is FY2024 - and the original pass omitted the entire second limb of s.1(1)(b), the KSH macro criteria that drive which settlements go into which package. MATERIAL CONTRADICTION, and the reason this signal is re-tagged: the original implies stated that 'Phase 2 supplier selection was legally locked by 28/02/2026, so the hardware/service contracts for the 31/12/2026 wave are already placed or being placed now' and concluded Printec 'must target the delivery, installation, cash-management and monitoring layers rather than a future tender'. That is wrong and would misdirect the sales approach. The 28/02/2026 deadline in s.3(3)(b) governs contracts BETWEEN obligated payment service providers under s.3(1)-(2) - joint installation, joint operation, and swapping or taking over settlement packages from each other. It has nothing to do with choosing an ATM vendor. This is confirmed by Annex 2 of the decree, whose ERA reporting fields are exactly: which provider is obligated under Annex 1, whether a joint-installation contract exists (yes/no), whether a joint-operation contract exists (yes/no), whether a swap/takeover contract exists (yes/no), which provider is obligated under that contract, and which provider files the data returns. There is no vendor field. Vendor selection is unregulated and remains commercially open - which is better news for Printec than the original framing, not worse. ALSO CORRECTED s.4(4): the original read it as 'reimburse the previous operator's demonstrated costs WITHIN 3 years'. The Hungarian is '3 even belul igazoltan felmerult koltsegeit megteriteni' - the 3-year window qualifies WHEN THE COSTS WERE INCURRED, not the payment deadline. ADDED three provisions the original missed: the 5-year minimum term on operation-takeover contracts (s.3(2)), the 3-yearly statutory reallocation (s.4(3)) and its first-review date (s.6). CORRECTED opp_size L -> M: on its own this is a mechanics/enabler signal whose distinct addressable value is the recurring site-transfer business; the large installation pipeline is already counted in the market-statistics and scoreboard signals and should not be double-counted here. IMPORTANT FINDING FOR THE OPERATOR REQUESTS: the original pass listed Annex 1 as an unobtainable gap, but the DECREE's Annex 1 - the master settlement-by-settlement allocation naming the obligated bank - is fully published in this consolidated text. Only the separate Annex 1 of the four MNB enforcement DECISIONS (the residual per-bank catch-up lists) remains unpublished. Kept despite the 'contradicted' tag because the corrected version is more valuable than the original.

verified_signals.entity: MNB banknote-validator and cash-machine availability regime (sector-wide)
verified_signals.signal: MNB decision H-KPL-I-B-5/2026 (07/05/2026) fines MBH Bank Nyrt. HUF 15,000,000 and imposes dated cash-handling obligations that restate sector-wide standards under MNB decree 1/2023 (I.17.): from 01/07/2026 forint banknotes may be recirculated through an ATM or customer-operated machine ONLY if authenticity and fitness were checked on a validator of a type on the MNB's published list AND running the exact hardware and software version specified there (s.4(2)); from 01/08/2026 the operator must maintain at least 98% availability as an annual average across its cash-machine network, excluding force majeure and seasonal operation (s.14(1)); plus branch and money-changer handling rules for category-A and damaged banknotes from 01/07/2026. MBH is NOT the only precedent: K&H Bank was ordered under the same decree by H-KPL-I-1/2025 (10/02/2025, no fine) and then fined HUF 60,000,000 by H-KPL-I-4/2025 (17/12/2025) for missing those deadlines.
verified_signals.source_name: MNB - H-KPL-I-B-5/2026 decision (PDF), cross-checked against the MNB register of authority decisions
verified_signals.implies: Two hard, dated, sector-wide compliance obligations land within weeks of each other: certified validator hardware AND software version control from 01/07/2026, and a measured 98% annual-average uptime obligation from 01/08/2026. Every one of the nine obligated banks needs validator firmware-version management, availability instrumentation and field-service SLAs to evidence compliance - a strong managed-services, monitoring and field-service proposition, and one where the enforcement record (HUF 60m and HUF 15m fines) makes the cost of non-compliance concrete and quotable in a pitch.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - the 01/08/2026 availability regime starts within days and the MNB has already fined two banks under this decree
verified_signals.followup: Pitch validator-version compliance and 98%-uptime SLA managed services to all nine obligated banks now, using the K&H HUF 60m and MBH HUF 15m fines as the cost-of-failure anchor; watch for the first availability-based enforcement once a full annual average can be measured.
verified_signals.verifier_note: Located the MBH decision by extracting the href from the MNB register rather than guessing the URL, then downloaded it (HTTP 200, 246,729 bytes) and extracted the text. CONFIRMED verbatim: fine 'a Hitelintezetet 15 000 000 Ft, azaz tizenotmillio forint osszegu birsag megfizetesere kotelezi', date 'Budapest, 2026. majus 07', the 01/07/2026 validator obligation under decree 1/2023 s.4(2) requiring an MNB-listed validator type 'az ott meghatarozott hardver- es szoftververzioval', and the 01/08/2026 obligation under s.14(1) for 'eves atlagban a legalabb 98%-os rendelkezesre allas' with the force-majeure and seasonal-operation carve-outs. So the regime description and the MBH figures the original pass reported are accurate. CONTRADICTED ON THE CENTRAL CLAIM, which is why this is re-tagged. The original signal was framed as a 'verified negative' asserting that 'MBH remains the only precedent for the MNB-listed-validator and availability regime' and that no K&H cash decision existed. Enumerating the MNB register turned up two earlier K&H decisions under the very same decree 1/2023, both of which I downloaded and read: H-KPL-I-1/2025 (dated 10/02/2025, measures only, no fine, obligations from 01/05/2025 and 01/08/2025 covering damaged-banknote acceptance, non-recirculation of category-A notes, and branch cash-desk service levels) and H-KPL-I-4/2025 (dated 17/12/2025, 'intezkedesek ismetelt alkalmazasa es birsag kiszabasa', imposing a fine of 60 000 000 Ft, i.e. HUF 60m, for failing to meet the first decision on time). The original pass's own operator note had flagged kh.hu as 403-blocked, but these decisions are hosted on mnb.hu and were reachable - they were simply missed because the search filtered on 2026 decisions only. The correction matters commercially: the largest cash-regime fine in this market is K&H's HUF 60m, four times MBH's, and there are two enforcement precedents rather than one, which strengthens rather than weakens the managed-services pitch. The narrow 2026-only negative does still hold - I re-enumerated the register and confirm the only 2026 H-KPL-I credit-institution decisions are CIB, Erste, OTP, UniCredit (all 25/03/2026) and MBH (07/05/2026). Note also that MNB decree 1/2023 as amended by 20/2025 is one of the instruments under constitutional challenge (see that signal), so this pipeline carries the same litigation risk.

verified_signals.signal: MNB decision H-KPL-I-4/2025 (17/12/2025) fines K&H Bank Zrt. HUF 60,000,000 - the largest cash-area fine in this cluster - for failing to meet on time the obligations imposed by H-KPL-I-1/2025 (10/02/2025), and RE-IMPOSES them from 01/03/2026 under MNB decree 1/2023 s.15/D: branch cash-desk (teller) customers must not be disadvantaged versus other customers in service level or waiting time. Concretely K&H must add at least one further staffed teller position in six named branches (Budapest Lechner Odon fasor 9, Margit krt 43-45, Andrassy ut 49; Kecskemet Nagykorosi ut 9/A; Szolnok Kossuth Lajos ut 18; Zalaegerszeg Kossuth utca 8) OR open teller positions in three currently teller-less branches in Budapest/Pest county plus one each in the county seats and one each in other settlements of Bacs-Kiskun, Jasz-Nagykun-Szolnok and Zala counties; extend online appointment booking for cash transactions to every branch with a teller on the same terms as other services, including the 12:00-13:00 window and the final hour before closing; and produce a monthly waiting-time monitoring report computed with the Mann-Whitney-Wilcoxon test. It had to report actions by 15/03/2026 and submit per-branch, per-ticket waiting-time data in minutes for March-May 2026 by 15/06/2026.
verified_signals.implies: A regulator has ordered a Hungarian bank to ADD physical cash-handling capacity and to instrument and statistically prove branch queue performance - the opposite of the branch-reduction trend, and a direct trigger for teller cash recyclers, branch cash automation, queue-management and appointment-booking systems, and waiting-time analytics. K&H is a proven repeat offender that has already been fined once for missing these deadlines, so the pressure to buy a demonstrable solution rather than a manual workaround is unusually high. The 15/06/2026 data submission means an MNB assessment - and a plausible third decision - is imminent.
verified_signals.likelihood: High - binding repeat order, obligations running from 01/03/2026, evidence already filed 15/06/2026 and under MNB assessment
verified_signals.followup: Approach K&H branch operations on queue management, appointment booking and teller cash automation ahead of the MNB's assessment of the 15/06/2026 submission; watch the MNB register for a third K&H cash decision. Also retrieve H-KPL-I-1/2025 for the original findings.

residual_gaps: SOURCES I COULD NOT REACH OR VERIFY. (1) The 'nearly 1,800 deposit-capable ATMs at end-Q1-2026, +14% YoY' figure carried by the original pass does NOT appear in the Bankmonitor article it was cited to. A search-engine snippet quotes the sentence, but I could not locate it in any page I actually retrieved (bankmonitor.hu x2, biztosdontes.hu, mfor.hu), so I stripped it. It should be recovered from the MNB penzforgalmi tablakeszlet before anyone uses it. (2) Two further figures in the original free-withdrawal signal - Q4-2025 average withdrawal size approaching HUF 120,000, and withdrawal transaction counts down 1.15 million YoY - appear in no source I retrieved and are stripped as unverified. (3) Annex 1 of the four MNB enforcement decisions of 25/03/2026 (the residual per-bank settlement catch-up lists) is omitted from the published web versions, so the exact remaining gap per bank still cannot be quantified from primary sources; a public-data request to the MNB remains the route. NOTE HOWEVER that the original pass's related gap is now CLOSED: Annex 1 of MNB decree 19/2025, the master settlement-by-settlement allocation naming the obligated bank for every affected settlement, IS fully published in the consolidated text on net.jogtar.hu and I used it to confirm the per-bank allocation totals. (4) kh.hu remains behind an Akamai 403 for both the fetch tool and desktop-UA curl, so K&H's own current deposit-ATM and automated-branch figures are still unconfirmed - but this mattered less than the original pass assumed, because the two K&H cash-enforcement decisions are hosted on mnb.hu and were retrievable there. (5) No ATM OEM or service vendor is named in any public Hungarian source for OTP, MBH, Erste, CIB, UniCredit or Granit. Vendor identification remains the single highest-value unsolved question in this cluster and is now more important, not less, given finding (7) below. (6) No 2026 edition of the MNB Fizetesi rendszer jelentes has been published, so the Q1-2026 ATM stock figures rest on press reporting of MNB statistics rather than the MNB publication itself; two independent outlets agree, which is why confidence is Medium rather than Low. (7) The original pass's claim that Phase 2 SUPPLIER contracts were legally locked by 28/02/2026 is wrong - that deadline governs inter-bank package-swap and obligation-takeover contracts, not vendor selection, which is unregulated and commercially open. The MNB ERA contract register would therefore NOT name winning suppliers, and requesting it is a lower-value ask than the original operator request implied. (8) Nothing new on OTP's eMACH.ai core deployment beyond the Dec-2023 contract; the alleged May-2026 contract remains unverified and is again not carried. (9) No ruling, case number or hearing date is public for the Constitutional Court challenge, which now appears to threaten BOTH the installation pipeline and the validator/availability pipeline, since the complaint also targets MNB decree 1/2023 as amended by 20/2025. VERIFICATION METHOD: all eight MNB and Raiffeisen decision PDFs were downloaded by desktop-UA curl and text-extracted locally with pdfminer.six, then checked phrase by phrase against the claims; all six press pages were fetched and parsed from raw HTML rather than trusted from summaries; the decree was read in full including both annexes; and the MNB register of authority decisions was enumerated and its hrefs extracted, which is how the missed K&H HUF 60m fine was found. CONFIDENCE IS CAPPED AT MEDIUM ON EVERY SIGNAL per the standing rule - only the Orchestrator may promote to High after cross-agent confirmation.
